We had to lower the topsails to save our rig, we were only pulling ourselves over with our fids on the heelings.

One other very interesting variation was seen on the main topsail rig. At the bottom of the mast there was the usual eye to let through a spare tack, and underneath this there was the normal wooden ‘heeling’ to fit through the topmast backstay holes.
The top-gallant yard can then be hoisted and fastened to the heeling.
The heelings were also cut away and replaced with short lengths.
When the rigging of a square-rigged ship is taken in, the rigging is secured to a heeling, which has an eye through which the rigging passes and secures it in its position with the aid of a fid.
